pages.lesson:
LESSON: THOUGHTS AND FEELINGS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation
Topic 1.2: Thoughts and feelings

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Thoughts and feelings. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: why it is good to be joyful, 1. How do you control your thoughts and feelings?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify good thoughts and feelings
2. explain the importance of being joyful

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THOUGHTS AND FEELINGS
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Thoughts and feelings helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: THOUGHTS AND FEELINGS
Study Thoughts and feelings like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify good thoughts and feelings

What this means
In this part you learn to identify good thoughts and feelings. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify good thoughts and feelings.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Thoughts and feelings” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify good thoughts and feelings. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the importance of being joyful

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the importance of being joyful. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the importance of being joyful.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Thoughts and feelings in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the importance of being joyful. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Thoughts and feelings is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Thoughts and feelings” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify good thoughts and feelings)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Thoughts and feelings in your own words. (skill: explain the importance of being joyful)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Thoughts and feelings to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify good thoughts and feelings.
3. Practise this skill: explain the importance of being joyful.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Thoughts and feelings from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Thoughts and feelings: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Thoughts and feelings?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. why it is good to be joyful, 1. How do you control your thoughts and feelings?
2. How do you cope with anger or sadness?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Thoughts and feelings means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify good thoughts and feelings.
5. Be able to: explain the importance of being joyful.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
